BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. HON. DAVID A. BIDO Mayor Municipality of Rosario Province of Northern Samar Dear Hon. Bido: This refers to your letter dated 17 May 2024, regarding your request for clarification on proceeding with piggery project sans Sanggunian Bayan Resolution authorizing acceptance of donation of land used. Per the representation, the local government unit of Rosario, Province of Northern Samar, included in its Annual Investment Plan, the development of pigpens for piggery projects. Correspondingly, to facilitate such, the local government unit, as represented by the local chief executive, acquired agricultural land through a Deed of Donation. However, prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan was not obtained, believing in good faith that it was not necessary, considering that the piggery project is funded under the Annual Investment Plan, and that the agricultural land used for the piggery project was donated, and no public funds were involved. Under this premise arose the request on whether or not the local government of Rosario, Northern Samar proceed with the piggery project without the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution authorizing the acceptance of the donation of the agricultural land. Foremost, we emphasize pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ", as amended ("LGC" for brevity), in relation to the requirement before a local chief executive ("LCE" for brevity), may enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit (LGU), to wit: "Sec. 22(c) — Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. Sec. 444(b)(I )(vi) — Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

Accordingly, this Department in Legal Opinion No. 22, Series of 2015 explained that: "The LCE may enter into contracts, for and in behalf of the municipality provided that either the following are present: I) if made upon authority of the sanqqunian concerned or 2) pursuant to law or ordinance. which means that if a law or ordinance already authorizes the LCE to enter into contract. prior authorization from the san unian concerned is notan more necessa . Such law or ordinance serves as an authority for the Mayor to enter such contract". Thus, before a local chief executive may enter into a contract, on behalf of the LGU, there must be either prior authorization from the sangguinan; or when there is a prior law or ordinance authorizing the LCE to enter into contract. In this regard, we deem it proper to highlight the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of "Municipality of Corella v. Philkonstrak" (G.R. No. 218663, February 28, 2022) citing the case of "Quisimbing v. Garcia" (G.R. No. 175527, December 8, 2008): In the landmark case of Quisumbing v. Garcia the Court delineated when a sangguniang bayan authorization is still necessary to accompany the appropriation ordinance and when it is not. Depending on the circumstances of the case, if the project is provided for in sufficient detail in the appropriation ordinance, meaning the transactions, bonds, contracts, documents, and other obligations the mayor would enter into in behalf of the municipality, among others, are enumerated, then no separate authorization is necessary. On the other hand, if the project is merely couched in general and generic terms, then a separate approval by the sangguniang bayan in accordance with the law is required. The recent case of Verceles, Jr. v. Commission on Audit (Verceles) citing Quisumbing, elaborated on this issue, thus: Explained simply, the LGC requires the local chief executive to secure prior authorization from the sanggunian before he can enter into contracts on behalf of the LGU. A separate prior authorization is no longer required if the specific protects are covered by appropriations of the LGU. The appropriation ordinance passed bv the sanqqunian is the local chief executive's authority to enter into a contract implementinq the project. As required in Quisumbing, the local chief executive must inquire if the provisions in the appropriation ordinance specifically covers the expense to be incurred or the contract to be entered into. If the project or program is identified in the appropriation ordinance in sufficient detail, then there is no more need to obtain a separate or additional authority from the sanggunian. In such case, the project and the cost are already identified and approved by the sanggunian through the appropriation ordinance. To require the local chief executive to secure another authorization for a project that has been specifically identified and approved by the sanggunian is antithetical to a responsive local govemment envisioned in the Constitution and in the LGC. Page 2 of 3

As the Verceles case explained, "sufficient authority" in an appropriation ordinance simply means specifically and expressly setting aside an amount of money for a certain project or program. In view of the foregoing, the appropriation ordinance approving the Annual Investment Plan of the LGU is controlling, in order to determine if there is a provision therein which specifically covers the contract to be entered into. Therefore, considering that the piggery project is funded under the Annual Investment Plan of the LGU of Rosario, and identified the program in sufficient detail, and not just in general or generic terms, we are of the considered view that the piggery project may proceed even without the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution authorizing the acceptance of the donation of agricultural land. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: o N VI R R. LLAMAS cretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs JVRULLLS-LRALLD/rjki copy FURNISHED. ARNEL M. AGABE.
